rv.q: This is British theatre operating at the very top of its game.

Trousers and ideas: they’re the twin, contrasting flavours of Stoppard’s busy, eccentric, dense farce, which manages to be on the one hand deeply absurd and silly and on the other extremely highminded and full of ideas.
The wit and larky intellectualism on display in Tom Stoppard’s 1974 play will have you smirking with pleasure.
Marber's finely calibrated revival gives a champagne effervescence to the densely plotted exchanges on Marxism, capitalism and the like, while the performances throughout are blissful.
My expectations ran high at the prospect of Travesties, and it does not disappoint.
Travesties both baffles and intrigues; a masterful piece of writing that will leave you thinking all the way home.

Equal part bonkers and fabulous it's like a Rubik's cube for the mind - with each turn you find yourself closer to the solution yet further away from the centre, and that's the joy of Stoppard's idiosyncrasy.
And this superb revival does the piece absolute justice.
What Patrick Marber has done in directing this revival...is make it more accessible by slowing it down...But in the process, for me, he has lost some of that runaway horse quality.
I felt alienated through out by how smugly pleased with itself the play is.
The triumph of this production is the way it honours Stoppard's dazzling intellect while also going full throttle with the piece's playful, sometimes bonkers, wit.

But together with textual revisions making this a newly-definitive production, with the cast re-moulding it and above all Hollander’s superbly faltering diffidence, this is the outstanding revival of a play in the West End this season.
Tom Hollander, fresh from The Night Manager , is dazzling and dazed as both the senior and muddled Carr and his younger more effervescent self.
Stoppard's dazzling intellectual and verbal jeu d'esprit is carried off by Tom Hollander and Freddie Fox, who play Henry Carr and Tristan Tzara respectively, with panache.
This is a slick production of Travesties with a starry cast who take all the play’s ridiculous elements and produce something very honourable.

cn.t: Critics praise this witty Stoppard revival as a dazzling intellectual workout, with Tom Hollander's performance earning near-universal acclaim. Some find the verbal pyrotechnics exhausting, but most agree it's brilliantly staged and sharply funny.
